ana-infra: Heads-up — night capacity swap in us-west1 tonight 02:00–05:00 PST. We'll rotate a cohort of ~120 GPUs (15-min cohorts) to apply NIC microcode + small kernel tweak. Expect up to ~10% reduction in UI-backed pool capacity while cohort is offline. Autoscale should cover obvious load but latency tail may spike. pinging @mike-sre @jake-oncall :eyes:

mike-sre: Can you drop the runbook and canary plan? also which pools exactly (reserved vs spot)? :thumbsup:

ana-infra: Runbook link: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/us-west1-cap-swap (TL;DR below). We'll avoid spot backfill during the window to minimize churn — only reserved and burst pools will be shifted. Canary: 3-node canary (low-traffic pool) first, then 5x 15-min cohorts.

jake-oncall: Dedicated customers? SLA hit risk?

ana-infra: Dedicated capacity pools (reserved contracts) are on separate racks and not touched. Public hosted pools may see degradation for small percentage of requests; we have fallback routing to eu and us-east for latency-sensitive routes. We'll enable circuit-breaker threshold at 450ms for text-gen routes and failover to next model variant if above. :warning:

sophia-telemetry: We should pre-seed KV/prefix caches after each cohort to avoid cold-start token penalties. Can we run cache-seed jobs?

ana-infra: Yes — preheat job queued 01:45 PST. Command we run on ops-runner: ```
# preview of ops commands
kubectl cordon gpu-node-03
kubectl drain gpu-node-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
./run_cache_seed --pool ui-backend --parallel 8
```

mike-sre: Also please annotate maintenance in the console and alerting so SREs don't double-schedule. Put a temporary schedule suppression for non-critical alerts during cohorts.

ops-bot: Maintenance scheduled by ana-infra for 9832105555: us-west1 capacity swap 02:00-05:00 PST. Pager suppression window set for non-critical alerts.

jake-oncall: I'll stand by at 01:30 and run quick perf checks after first cohort. If latency >10% tail, we'll abort and rollback.

ana-infra: Plan note on cost tradeoffs — avoiding spot churn increases short-term run cost (est +$650 for the window) but reduces risk of repeated evictions and extra cache-warm cycles. Logging will capture token-level cost impact. :money_with_wings:

sophia-telemetry: I'll add a short eval run (1000 requests) post-cohort to validate model quality and latency.

mike-sre: SGTM. Please post status updates in this thread as cohorts finish. :thumbsup:

ana-infra: will do. First cohort start @ 02:00 PST. Updates every 15m or on any anomaly.
